topic: Local treatment-factor detectability and ATT absorption in full-sample interactive fixed effects. For triangular rectangular panels with N/T in a compact subset of (0,infinity), iid Gaussian noise sigma in [sigma_min,sigma_max], a fixed-rank strong baseline Lambda F^T, block treatment D=dq^T, and treatment-supported heterogeneity delta_NT(d elementwise a)(q elementwise b)^T at delta_NT=theta/sqrt(min(N,T)), impose exact finite-array orthogonality to the baseline factor spaces, bounded nonzero supported means and variances, and positive full plus untreated/pre-period restricted Gram limits. Define the full-sample coefficient as the smallest beta in the compact-domain rank-(r+1) profiled least-squares argmin. Derive its uniform ATT absorption law as the explicit noise-normalized 2-by-2 spiked-SVD profile, including critical selections, prove undercoverage of the explicitly residualized conventional IFE Wald interval on a nonempty transition region, and construct rank-r masked-cell imputation with studentized coverage uniform over theta in a fixed compact interval. Consumer: Gobillon--Magnac's enterprise-zone full-sample Bai-IFE workflow. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: After strong-factor removal, the coefficient profile reduces to B(x)=sqrt(max(c,1)pq){h[[mu_a mu_b,mu_a sqrt(v_b)],[sqrt(v_a)mu_b,sqrt(v_a v_b)]]-x e11} and Phi(x)=||B(x)||_F^2-psi_c(s1(B(x))). A unique no-absorption minimizer is proved on a nonzero subcritical region; the replicated witness has checked edge theta/sigma=2/3 and local large-signal absorption expansion. Checks covered zero heterogeneity, spectral crossing, coefficient escape, rectangular normalization, and current weak-factor literature, which excludes this rank-one treatment regressor. For the replicated geometry, the limiting potential is strictly separated below the edge. A 20,000-geometry search found no multiple local minima on the ATT-to-rank-one interval, while small Gaussian panels exposed finite-size variability but no normalization contradiction; exact orthogonality also confirms that masked validity alone is not the novelty. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove uniform global argmin localization and selection for the random profiled criterion, including uniqueness/separation or the correct law at every genuine tie. EARLY KILL TEST: Certify the explicit scalar profile's stationary/global-minimizer structure; if admissible opposite m^(-1/4) perturbations around a separated global tie yield different selections with identical limiting nuisance coordinates, pivot or stop. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/panel_ife_heterospike_phase.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Does full-sample rank-(r+1) Bai-IFE profiling with treatment-supported local rank-one heterogeneity admit a uniform global-argmin and selection law over compact signal-to-noise ratios and rectangular aspect ratios, including BBP-edge and exact-tie regimes?

source_refs.claim: The enterprise-zone application directly compares Bai whole-sample interactive-effects estimation with counterfactual and synthetic-control methods.
source_refs.author: Laurent Gobillon and Thierry Magnac

source_refs.claim: Finite-rank additive perturbations of rectangular noise have an explicit singular-value and singular-vector detectability transition, but the spike is fixed rather than indexed by a profiled regression coefficient.
source_refs.author: Florent Benaych-Georges and Raj Rao Nadakuditi

source_refs.claim: Conventional IFE estimators and confidence intervals can be heavily biased and size-distorted under weak factors, motivating uniform analysis in factor strength.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong, Martin Weidner, and Andrei Zeleneev

open_problems.why_unsolved: Bai-type panel theory profiles the regression coefficient under regular strong-factor conditions, while rectangular-spike theory analyzes a fixed perturbation and Armstrong-Weidner-Zeleneev obtain robustness without resolving the coefficient-specific absorption map. Here changing beta changes the spike itself, so the leading singular-value process must be controlled uniformly over beta and coupled to an argmin operation. The literature scan located no proof of global localization, separation, or measurable selection for this endogenously profiled spiked-SVD objective; at a genuine deterministic tie, ordinary uniform convergence does not determine which coefficient the random criterion selects.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit deterministic 2-by-2 spiked-SVD profile with uniform epi-convergence and global argmin localization, a characterization of unique and tied minimizers over the full compact parameter domain, and the random selection law at every genuine tie.

writing_exemplar.why: Its progression from regional-policy confounding to whole-sample IFE and counterfactual alternatives is the closest application-facing framing for the enterprise-zone consumer.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Regional policies face latent region-specific responses to common shocks -> ordinary DiD is generically biased -> whole-sample Bai-IFE is used in the enterprise-zone workflow -> treatment-supported heterogeneity may itself become the extra fitted factor at the spectral detection boundary.

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce rectangular finite-rank perturbation eigen-equations to a finite matrix-valued determinant and use the rectangular D-transform to characterize outlier singular values and vector overlaps.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After strong-factor removal, every fixed coefficient value produces a finite-rank rectangular signal-plus-noise problem; the missing step is to make the spectral argument uniform in the coefficient and pass it through argmin selection.

method_exemplars.technique: Analyze near-critical spiked eigenvalues through a stochastic-operator limit whose boundary condition is indexed by the local spike.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a model for non-Gaussian critical selection laws when deterministic spike separation disappears, although the panel problem additionally profiles over a continuum of coefficient-indexed rectangular spikes.

method_exemplars.technique: Use perturbation expansions of the profiled least-squares objective to establish coefficient limit theory when the fitted factor count exceeds the true count.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The estimator is the same profiled IFE least-squares object, but the treatment-aligned factor at the random-matrix threshold falls outside the regular over-factoring regime.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the exact asymptotic coverage surface of the explicitly residualized conventional Bai-IFE Wald interval when treatment-supported heterogeneous effects enter at the rectangular spiked-SVD scale, and on which open transition region is coverage strictly below nominal?

source_refs.claim: Bai derives consistency and limiting distributions for profiled interactive-effects regression coefficients under the regular large-N, large-T factor model.
source_refs.author: Jushan Bai

source_refs.claim: Weak factors can make existing IFE confidence intervals heavily size-distorted; bias-aware intervals are proposed to remain uniformly valid in factor strength.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong, Martin Weidner, and Andrei Zeleneev

source_refs.claim: IFE regressions with heterogeneous effects converge to variance-weighted treatment-effect estimands, while inference is identified as a remaining challenge.
source_refs.author: Artūras Juodis and Martin Weidner

open_problems.why_unsolved: The regular Bai expansion centers the coefficient around a fixed homogeneous slope, whereas the local heterogeneous component here can be partially or fully absorbed by the additional fitted factor. Armstrong-Weidner-Zeleneev establish that weak factors cause size distortion and construct robust intervals, but do not give the explicit coverage phase diagram for a treatment-aligned block factor or the law of a conventionally studentized, residualized Bai estimator. Juodis-Weidner clarify that heterogeneous-slope IFE limits are weighted estimands but leave inference open. The obstacle is a nonregular joint limit: the numerator depends on global argmin selection while the conventional residual variance treats the selected factor space as regular.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A joint weak limit for the selected coefficient and its conventional residualized standard error, an explicit coverage function of signal-to-noise ratio, aspect ratio, and support moments, and a proof of coverage below 1-alpha on a nonempty open transition region with separate formulas at critical selections.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames weak factors through the empirical failure of conventional IFE confidence intervals and makes uniform coverage, rather than pointwise asymptotics, the inferential target.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: IFE regression is attractive for latent panel confounding -> standard asymptotics rely on factors being sufficiently strong -> weak factors generate bias and size distortion -> a treatment-aligned local factor calls for an explicit coverage phase diagram for the conventional enterprise-zone Wald workflow.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine minimax-linear debiasing with a data-dependent nuclear-norm bound on latent-effect estimation error to form bias-aware confidence intervals uniform in factor strength.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest uniform-in-weakness inference result for an IFE regression coefficient and provides the natural benchmark against which the conventional-Wald coverage surface should be compared.

method_exemplars.technique: Profile least squares over low-rank interactive effects and derive a residualized asymptotic linear representation with bias correction and variance estimation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the conventional estimator and Wald construction whose expansion must be recomputed after the local heterogeneous treatment component makes factor selection nonregular.

method_exemplars.technique: Obtain local-to-critical spike limit laws rather than substituting either subcritical edge or supercritical Gaussian approximations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Coverage at the absorption boundary depends on the same failure of regular Gaussian spectral asymptotics, now composed with coefficient selection and studentization.

open_problems.open_problem: Can rank-r masked-cell factor imputation yield a studentized ATT interval with coverage uniform over a compact local-heterogeneity amplitude while the corresponding full-sample rank-(r+1) IFE estimator crosses an absorption transition?

source_refs.claim: Tall-wide factor imputation gives asymptotic normality for average and individual treatment effects but assumes strong factor structure in the full panel and relevant observed subblocks.
source_refs.author: Jushan Bai and Serena Ng
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Causal matrix completion imputes untreated potential outcomes from untreated unit-period cells and accommodates structured treatment-induced missingness.
source_refs.author: Susan Athey, Mohsen Bayati, Nikolay Doudchenko, Guido W. Imbens, and Khashayar Khosravi
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Counterfactual IFE imputation is reported to correct bias of whole-sample IFE under heterogeneous treatment effects, subject to correct specification and adequate untreated dimensions.
source_refs.author: Yiqing Xu

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing imputation results establish pointwise normal theory under strong baseline factors and appropriate observed-block Gram conditions, and Xu documents the benefit of excluding treated outcomes when effects are heterogeneous. They do not connect that validity to a simultaneous local sequence in which the same heterogeneous treatment component is detectable and absorbable in a full-sample extra-factor fit. Uniformity requires controlling factor and loading estimation and studentization over the entire compact amplitude, including values at which the competing full-sample criterion changes minimizer; the scan located no joint theorem proving masked coverage and full-sample failure on the same triangular array.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform asymptotic linear representation and studentized Gaussian limit for the rank-r masked ATT estimator over compact local amplitudes, a uniformly consistent variance estimator, and a comparison theorem showing nominal masked coverage alongside full-sample Wald undercoverage on the absorption transition region.

writing_exemplar.why: Its observed-block-to-missing-cell narrative directly frames masked factor recovery, counterfactual imputation, and ATT inference.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Treatment hides untreated potential outcomes in a block of the panel -> strong latent-factor structure permits recovery from tall and wide untreated blocks -> imputed counterfactuals yield ATT normal theory -> local treatment-supported heterogeneity requires coverage uniformity precisely where full-sample factor fitting can absorb ATT.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate factors from a tall observed block and loadings from a wide observed block, re-rotate the estimates, and derive entrywise and averaged asymptotic representations for imputed common components.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed masked estimator has the same block geometry and rank-r target; the new proof must make its ATT expansion and variance approximation uniform in the local heterogeneous-effect amplitude.

method_exemplars.technique: Cross-fit matrix-completion predictions and combine outcome imputation with inverse-probability weighting to obtain a parametric-rate mean-zero Gaussian expansion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Cross-fitting offers a concrete route to decouple low-rank nuisance estimation from the ATT score if direct masked-PC remainder bounds are not uniform enough.

method_exemplars.technique: Use nuclear-norm regularization on observed untreated cells and empirical-process bounds adapted to treatment-induced time-series missingness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies an alternative low-rank imputation route under the same block-missing causal target and can benchmark whether fixed-rank masked PC needs stronger Gram assumptions than regularized completion.

open_problems.open_problem: Which support-moment and signal-strength conditions separate harmless over-fitting from ATT absorption when the extra factor in Moon-Weidner profiled IFE is a treatment-aligned local factor rather than an irrelevant regular factor?

source_refs.claim: Under its assumptions, the IFE slope limit distribution is invariant to using more factors than the true number, so consistent factor-count selection is unnecessary when rank is not underestimated.
source_refs.author: Hyungsik Roger Moon and Martin Weidner

source_refs.claim: With weakly influential factors and proportional dimensions, principal-component directions are inconsistent and undergo a threshold below which the estimated direction becomes uninformative.
source_refs.author: Alexei Onatski

source_refs.claim: Local factors affecting subsets of units generate a continuum of factor strengths, and relevance and estimability depend on pervasiveness and eigenvector information.
source_refs.author: Simon Freyaldenhoven

source_refs.claim: Under heterogeneous effects, IFE panel slopes can represent variance-weighted rather than unweighted treatment effects, making regressor-factor geometry consequential for the estimand.
source_refs.author: Artūras Juodis and Martin Weidner

open_problems.why_unsolved: Moon-Weidner's over-factoring invariance is a regular perturbation result, while Onatski and Freyaldenhoven show that weak or subset-supported factors have qualitatively different eigenvector behavior. Neither line treats an extra factor constructed from treatment support and heterogeneous effects, whose left and right means give it direct overlap with the treatment regressor. That overlap lets profiling trade off coefficient movement against low-rank fit, violating the intuition that an unused extra factor is asymptotically harmless. The scan found no characterization in terms of treated share, post share, supported means and variances, restricted Gram limits, and local spike strength.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Necessary-and-sufficient or sharp sufficient support-moment conditions for over-factoring invariance, an explicit absorption boundary when those conditions fail, and counterexamples showing distinct coefficient limits on opposite sides of the boundary.

writing_exemplar.why: Its practical claim that overestimating factor rank need not affect slope inference supplies the precise benchmark whose boundary must be redrawn for treatment-aligned local factors.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: The true number of interactive effects is unknown -> practitioners often fit an upper bound on rank -> regular over-fitting leaves slope inference unchanged -> a local factor supported exactly on treated post-period cells may instead absorb heterogeneous ATT.

method_exemplars.technique: Expand the profiled low-rank least-squares objective under excess fitted rank and show that regular extra-factor terms do not enter the first-order coefficient law.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired boundary theorem begins by isolating the exact perturbation step where treatment-factor overlap prevents the usual over-rank remainder from being negligible.

method_exemplars.technique: Use Marchenko-Pastur resolvents to derive probability limits and asymptotic laws for weak-factor principal components above and below their detectability threshold.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The extra treatment factor is at the same proportional-dimension weak-spike scale, but its coefficient-dependent alignment adds a regression estimand to the spectral transition.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine eigenvalue growth with eigenvector partial sums to distinguish local-factor relevance from principal-component estimability.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Treatment support is a known local subset, so its support sums and eigenvector mass are natural statistics for expressing when the local factor is harmless, detectable, or coefficient-absorbing.

literature_map:
Bai (2009, Econometrica) supplies the canonical large-N, large-T profiled least-squares IFE coefficient and conventional limit theory.
Gobillon and Magnac (2016, Review of Economics and Statistics) apply whole-sample Bai IFE, counterfactual IFE, and synthetic controls to French enterprise zones.
Moon and Weidner (2015, Econometrica) show slope inference can be invariant to overestimating factor rank under regular assumptions.
Onatski (2012, Journal of Econometrics) shows weak-factor PCs are inconsistent and exhibit a proportional-dimension detectability threshold.
Freyaldenhoven (2022, Journal of Econometrics) formalizes local factors supported on subsets and separates economic relevance from PC estimability.
Benaych-Georges and Nadakuditi (2012, Journal of Multivariate Analysis) give rectangular additive-spike outlier and singular-vector overlap formulas.
Bloemendal and Virág (2013, Probability Theory and Related Fields) derive near-critical real spiked-matrix laws, highlighting nonregular edge behavior.
Armstrong, Weidner, and Zeleneev (2026, Journal of Political Economy) prove weak factors can heavily bias IFE coefficients and distort conventional CI size, then construct uniform bias-aware CIs.
Juodis and Weidner (2026, arXiv:2604.18078) interpret latent-factor panel slopes under heterogeneity as variance-weighted treatment effects and identify inference as challenging.
Xu (2017, Political Analysis) reports that counterfactual IFE imputation corrects whole-sample IFE bias under heterogeneous treatment effects, conditional on correct specification.
Bai and Ng (2021, JASA) give tall-wide factor imputation and normal theory for ATT under strong full-panel and observed-block factors.
Athey et al. (2021, JASA) formulate causal panel estimation as nuclear-norm completion of untreated potential outcomes under structured missingness.
Abadie, Agarwal, Dwivedi, and Shah (2024, arXiv:2402.11652) combine cross-fitted matrix completion and weighting for parametric-rate Gaussian causal inference.
The unresolved junction is coefficient-indexed spike selection: random-matrix papers fix the spike, while panel papers do not derive the explicit ATT-absorption argmin or conventional-Wald coverage phase diagram.
